case: Epic Sepsis Model at Michigan Medicine (R2, with inside reference)
evidenceBase: Wong et al. 2021, JAMA Intern Med 181(8):1065-1070 (Michigan Medicine, 6 Dec 2018 - 20 Oct 2019; 38,455 hospitalizations) - hospital's own outcome data, class O per Section 6.1
Bennett et al. 2019, arXiv:1902.07276 (UCHealth, 5 hospitals, Jun-Oct 2017; Epic co-author) - published, class D

Inside reference (R2): Epic's internal documentation as reported by Wong et al. 2021 - AUC 0.76-0.83 reported by Epic; model developed on data from 405,000 patient encounters across 3 health systems; documents described as "confidential, non-peer-reviewed model performance documents", seen by the authors with permission

ratings.criterion: Low accuracy could cause damage

plan.measure: A: Sensitivity and false-alert rate at the operating threshold
plan.measureRationale: Missed sepsis and alert fatigue both depend on error rates at the threshold in use (score 6 or more); AUC hides that trade-off.
plan.acceptanceCriterion: At the operating threshold: sensitivity at least 0.61 and PPV at least 0.33, the early-warning-score baseline in Bennett et al. (2019), published before the cut-off.

ratings.evidence: O: Wong et al. 2021, hospitalization-level sensitivity 33%, specificity 83%, PPV 12%, NPV 95% at a score of 6 or more; a score of 6 or more occurred in 18% of hospitalizations (6,971 of 38,455). Inside reference: Epic reported AUC 0.76-0.83.
ratings.argument: Sensitivity 0.33 and PPV 0.12 are both below the registered baseline, so the expected elements are shown not met (G4). The data are the hospital's own patients at its own threshold, so they are attributable to the deployed system. The inside reference reports a higher AUC than the hospital measured; it does not report the registered measure at this hospital, so the rating stands.

ratings.evidence: D: Bennett et al. 2019 states the model was developed on data from three health systems; it does not describe those populations. Inside reference: the model was developed on 405,000 patient encounters across 3 health systems (Epic documentation, as reported by Wong et al. 2021).
ratings.argument: Size and number of sites are not a description of the training population, so the match with this hospital's patients still cannot be shown (G4). The requirement narrows to the population description.

ratings.criterion: Low reliability or reproducibility could cause damage; contexts tested

plan.measure: A: Error rates by site, period or condition
plan.measureRationale: Whether performance carries over from the published site to this hospital decides reliance.
plan.acceptanceCriterion: Hospitalization-level AUC at this hospital no more than 0.05 below the AUC published before the cut-off (0.73, Bennett et al. 2019).

ratings.evidence: O: Wong et al. 2021, hospitalization-level AUC 0.63 (95% CI 0.62-0.64). D: Bennett et al. 2019, AUC 0.73 at UCHealth. Inside reference: Epic reported AUC 0.76-0.83.
ratings.argument: 0.63 is 0.10 below 0.73, beyond the registered margin, so the element is shown not met. The two studies may define the unit of analysis differently; that weakens the comparison. Wong's time-horizon AUCs (0.72-0.76) would meet the margin, but Wong et al. explain that they overstate performance because they treat each prediction as independent; the registered measure is the hospitalization-level AUC. The inside reference reports a higher AUC than the hospital measured; it does not report the registered measure at this hospital, so the rating stands.

ratings.evidence: O: Wong et al. 2021 analysed the model's scores as generated in the hospital's records for 38,455 hospitalizations. D: Bennett et al. 2019 (February 2019), validation at UCHealth.
ratings.argument: Both expected elements are shown met. Bennett et al. has an Epic co-author, which the argument notes but which does not remove it as a validation.
